0.0.n: This country name sets the location for his appearances.

0.2.n: Highlights Japan as the setting, potentially contrasting it with other places.

0.3.n: Names the role he takes when appearing in the media.

0.4.n: Follows a noun to identify someone's role or capacity.

0.5.n: 出演する means to appear in a show or broadcast; here it joins たり to list an example.

0.6.n: With a past-form verb, たり presents an activity as one example rather than a complete list.

1.0.n: A shortened form of プロフェッショナル, referring here to his status in golf.

1.1.n: Identifies the capacity in which he takes on golf.

1.2.n: This borrowed sports name is the activity he takes on.

1.3.n: Marks the challenge being attempted with 挑戦する.

1.4.n: Adds golf to his other activities.

1.5.n: The linking form of 挑戦する connects this activity to the next clause.

2.0.n: 充実する becomes 充実した before a noun, describing a state of richness or satisfaction.

2.1.n: Refers to his everyday way of living, not biological life.

2.2.n: Marks 生活 as what he is spending or living.

2.3.n: 過ごす in the ている form describes how he is currently spending his life.

2.4.n: Turns the preceding statement into a noun-like unit that can be the subject.

2.5.n: Marks the fact about his life as what comes across to the observer.

2.6.n: 伝わる + てくる suggests an impression reaching us; ます makes it polite.

2.7.n: Invites the listener to share the speaker's impression.

3.0.n: 所属する in the ている form describes ongoing membership and directly modifies ゴルフクラブ.

3.1.n: Here this means a membership organization, not a piece of golfing equipment.

3.2.n: Marks the golf club as the thing whose location is being described.

3.3.n: This is the first part of the place name アナハイム, split by the subtitle tokenizer.

3.4.n: Completes the place name アナハイム; it is not a separate word here.

3.5.n: Marks Anaheim as the comparison partner for 同じ.

3.6.n: 同じ directly modifies オレンジ郡 without な.

3.7.n: This is a place name; 郡 means county.

3.8.n: Marks the location where the club exists.

3.9.n: The linking form of ある continues the sentence instead of ending it.

4.0.n: プホルス is a surname; 氏 is a respectful title commonly used in reporting.

4.1.n: Lists examples, leaving room for other members not named here.

4.2.n: This is the baseball player's surname, followed by the title 選手.

4.3.n: Used after an athlete's name as a respectful identifying title.

4.4.n: Adds these players to the people who belong to the club.

4.5.n: 所属しており is a formal linking version of 所属している, describing ongoing membership.

5.0.n: This shortened borrowed word refers to time outside the playing season.

5.1.n: Marks the time when they played together.

5.2.n: Highlights the off-season as the time frame.

5.3.n: Combines with the following に to describe doing an activity with others.

5.4.n: Makes 一緒に describe how they played their rounds.

5.5.n: Past form of 回る, which in golf means going around the course.

5.6.n: After a past-form verb, こと combines with がある to express previous experience.

5.7.n: Links the past experience expressed by こと to ある.

5.8.n: In verb + ことがある, it indicates that someone has done something before.

5.9.n: よう indicates an inference rather than a direct, definite assertion.

5.10.n: Makes the statement ending in よう polite.

6.0.n: Names the field contrasted with his other areas of activity.

6.1.n: Sets a limit that the following でなく rejects.

6.2.n: This is part of でなく, the linking negative of だ, not the particle marking location.

6.3.n: Combines with だけで to make だけでなく, meaning not only.

6.4.n: 後 attached to 引退 indicates the period following his retirement.

6.5.n: Emphasizes that his activities continue after retirement too.

6.6.n: Describes variety and takes な before the noun 分野.

6.7.n: Connects 様々 to the noun it describes.

6.8.n: Refers to areas of work or activity, not physical playing fields.

6.9.n: Marks the areas in which he is active.

6.10.n: The plain form directly modifies the following person's name, describing his successful involvement.

6.11.n: This is his surname, placed before his given name in Japanese.

6.12.n: This character begins the given name 滋利; the tokenizer has split the name.

6.13.n: 利 completes the given name 滋利, and さん is a respectful title; this is not a verb.

7.0.n: Indicates the speaker wants another opportunity to hear such an interview.

7.1.n: Names the language used in the interview.

7.2.n: Marks the language used to conduct the interview.

7.3.n: Lets 英語で modify インタビュー, forming an interview conducted in English.

7.4.n: This borrowed noun is what the speaker wants to hear.

7.5.n: Marks the interview as what the speaker wants to listen to.

7.6.n: 聞く becomes 聞きたい to express desire; です adds politeness.

7.7.n: Invites agreement with the speaker's wish rather than asking a direct question.

0.lit: In Japan, as a commentator, appearing among other activities,
0.tip: Verb + たり lists representative activities rather than every activity.

1.lit: As a professional, taking on golf too,
1.tip: The ending し here links clauses; it is the connecting form of する.

2.lit: The fact that he is spending a fulfilling life comes across to us, doesn't it?
2.tip: こと turns the whole description of his life into the thing that comes across.

3.lit: The golf club he belongs to is in the same Orange County as Anaheim, and,
3.tip: 所属している comes before ゴルフクラブ and tells you which club is meant.

4.lit: Mr. Pujols and player Arenado, among others, also belong, and,
4.tip: しており is a formal way to link a statement using している to what follows.

5.lit: During the off-season, it seems they have had the experience of playing a round together.
5.tip: Past-form verb + ことがある expresses having done something before.

6.lit: Not only baseball, even after retirement, active in various fields: Mr. Shigetoshi Hasegawa.
6.tip: This line ends with a name, with the preceding description modifying that person rather than forming a complete sentence.

7.lit: Again, an interview in English, we want to hear, don't we?
7.tip: での lets a phrase like 英語で describe a noun: an interview in English.
